title: The Pinnacle Architecture with fixed connectivity of degree eight
authors: Paul Webster, Tom Peham, Lawrence Z. Cohen
abstract: We show how the Pinnacle architecture can be adapted to be compatible with superconducting qubits, where the connectivity between qubits must be fixed at fabrication. Specifically, we present a modified instantiation of the architecture that has fixed connectivity degree of eight. With this instantiation, we show that a 2048-bit RSA integer can be factored in one month with approximately 120 000 physical qubits, given a physical error rate of $10^{-3}$, code cycle time of 1 microsecond and reaction time of 10 microseconds.
summary: This paper details the adaptation of the Pinnacle quantum computing architecture for superconducting qubits, which inherently have fixed connectivity. By developing the 'Frozen Pinnacle Architecture' with a fixed connectivity degree of eight, the authors demonstrate a viable pathway to factor 2048-bit RSA integers using about 120,000 physical qubits in one month.
main_problem: The core challenge is adapting the high-level Pinnacle quantum computation architecture to the physical constraints of superconducting qubits, specifically the requirement for fixed qubit connectivity.
main_result: The modified 'Frozen Pinnacle Architecture' successfully supports the factoring of a 2048-bit RSA integer within one month using approximately 120,000 physical qubits.
method: The authors modified the architecture by using specific gadgets and relying on cyclic shift automorphisms to implement necessary logical Pauli measurements while strictly maintaining a fixed connectivity degree of eight.
model_or_system: The system is based on superconducting qubits and utilizes the generalized bicycle (GB) code, implemented through interconnected 'gadget systems' and 'processing blocks' to achieve fault-tolerant quantum computation.
key_observables: Factoring time (one month), physical qubit count (120,000), and the fixed connectivity degree (eight).
important_parameters: Physical error rate ($10^{-3}$), code cycle time ($1 \mu s$), and reaction time ($10 \mu s$).
main_assumptions: The resource estimate assumes a runtime limit of one month, and the analysis relies on extrapolating simulation results for larger code distances using an ansatz.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the baseline vs. frozen architecture qubit counts. Figure 2 shows the per-block logical error rate vs. code distance for various measurement components.
paper_structure: The paper details the architectural modification to enforce fixed connectivity, describes the implementation of complex operations like memory access and Toffoli gates using specific automorphisms, and concludes with a resource estimation for RSA-2048 factoring.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, resource-estimated roadmap for scaling quantum computation on superconducting hardware by solving the critical issue of fixed connectivity, which is a major bottleneck in realizing large-scale quantum processors.
